questions.q: Calculate the total size of the council if cabinet has ... and state ministers are .... Use the method 'Cabinet Decision Making'. Work with: cabinet_members = 512, state_ministers = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total.

Find the total number of ministers given ... cabinet and ... state ministers. Use the method 'Cabinet Decision Making'. Work with: cabinet_members = 2048, state_ministers = 150. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total.
Explain in your own words what 'Cabinet Decision Making' refers to.
questions.a: The process where a group of senior ministers makes major policy decisions collectively in the name of the Council of Ministers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cabinet Decision Making'.
questions.a: Collective responsibility of the inner ring of ministers for government policy.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Cabinet Decision Making', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the maximum days Rajya Sabha can delay a money bill. Use the method 'Parliamentary Budget Delay'. Work with: limit = 14. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of limit.
How many days can the upper house hold a budget bill? Use the method 'Parliamentary Budget Delay'. Work with: limit = 14. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of limit.
Explain in your own words what 'Parliamentary Budget Delay' refers to.
questions.a: The period during which the Rajya Sabha can hold up a money bill passed by the Lok Sabha before it must be returned.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Parliamentary Budget Delay'.
questions.a: Lok Sabha holds supreme power in money matters, limiting Rajya Sabha to a 14-day delay.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Parliamentary Budget Delay', in plain ASCII form.
Calculate the months a non-MP minister has to get elected. Use the method 'Ministerial Tenure'. Work with: months = 6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of months.
How many months are allowed for a minister to join parliament? Use the method 'Ministerial Tenure'. Work with: months = 6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of months.
Explain in your own words what 'Ministerial Tenure' refers to.
questions.a: The time limit within which a non-member appointed as a minister must get elected to either House of Parliament.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Ministerial Tenure'.
questions.a: Ministers must secure democratic legitimacy through election within six months.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Ministerial Tenure', in plain ASCII form.
